title: Iceland and the Greenland-Iceland-Faroe Ridge
description: Basin edit contract for Iceland. Four cited operations in two Cao et al. (2017) map intervals: the subaerial Upper Tertiary lava plateau at 11-2 Ma, drawn as the dissolved 'gold' outcrop of the Natturufraedistofnun Islands 1:600,000 bedrock map, and its three oldest flanks at 20-11 Ma, drawn as the same outcrop clipped to the NW peninsula, Trollaskagi and the Eastfjords. Each add-land carries a paired remove-shallow so the evidence record stops asserting Cao's shallow-marine class under ground the layer now calls land. Designed in docs/research/palaeo-coastlines-iceland-ne-atlantic.md; the geometry is derived by scripts/research/palaeo_coastlines_iceland_ops.py and is not hand-edited.

window.reason: Iceland, its insular shelf, the Greenland-Iceland Ridge and the western Iceland-Faroe Ridge. The eastern edge stops at -12 E, west of the Faroe Platform, so that nothing in this contract can touch the Faroes; the same window simplification.json protects from node reduction

editorial: EarthHistory modification after the references listed in this contract

ops.rationale: Cao 2017 draws no landmass anywhere over Iceland at 11-2 Ma: the whole island and its insular shelf carry the shallow-marine class and nothing else, so on screen the North Atlantic has no Iceland at any Neogene age. Iceland's own Tertiary lava pile contradicts that. The Natturufraedistofnun Islands 1:600,000 bedrock map classes 35,643 km2 of present outcrop as 'Basic and intermediate extrusive rocks with ingercalated sediments. Upper Tertiary, older than 3.3 m.y.', and the published descriptions of that pile are subaerial flood basalts; Harardarson et al. (2008) put the Tertiary area at about 36,000 km2 independently. The palaeobotanical record is continuous across the bin and includes the 9-8 Ma and 5.5 Ma transatlantic dispersals Denk et al. (2010) date. The operation draws that outcrop as land. Three things it is not. It is not a reconstructed coastline: the outcrop is a MINIMUM footprint, because erosion, burial under younger lavas, glacial excavation and subsidence all remove area, so the true island was wider - a defensible bracket runs from this 35,643 km2 to the 101,155 km2 modern outline, and the contract deliberately draws the minimum. It is not a statement about the neovolcanic zones, which are excluded although old crust underlies them, so the drawn island has a hole down its middle. And its age cut is 3.3 Ma, the finest the source offers and 1.3 Myr older than the bin's 2.01 Ma young bound, which makes the footprint a slight under-claim rather than an over-claim.
ops.claimOrInference: The subaerial character and the older-than-3.3 Ma age of the mapped units are claims of the sources. That this makes Cao's shallow-marine class wrong for 11-2 Ma over that footprint, and the choice to draw the present outcrop as land, are EarthHistory inferences.
ops.editorial: EarthHistory modification after Saemundsson (1979), Harardarson et al. (2008), the NI 1:600,000 bedrock map and, for the 20-11 lobes, the published Icelandic radiometric age localities

ops.rationale: The paired removal for the 11-2 add-land. Cao classes the whole island shallow marine, and land is drawn above shallow sea anyway, so on screen the removal changes nothing. It exists so the evidence record is honest: without it the layer would still carry 'Cao et al. (2017) shallow marine' under ground it now calls land, and the map key would list a claim the operation contradicts. The ring is identical to the add-land.

ops.rationale: The same absence at 20-11 Ma, with a much weaker geometry, and the contract has to say so. No exposed crust anywhere in Iceland is older than about 16 Ma, so the 16.3-20 Ma half of this 9 Myr bin has NO mapped land at all and this operation is a young-end statement only. The geometry is the same 'gold' outcrop restricted to the three lobes the published radiometric ages place at or above 12-16 Ma: the NW peninsula (Vestfirdir, >15 Ma at the exposed top and about 16 Ma at the deepest exposed level), Trollaskagi in the north (about 12 Ma) and the Eastfjords (13-14 Ma, 'just over 13 m.y.' at the oldest locality). The bounding rectangles are selectors ON the outcrop, not an outline of the island: the emitted rings are the mapped outcrop boundary clipped by them. The northern lobe is the weak one - 12 Ma is inside the bin but only just - and it is named here rather than quietly included. Two model artefacts travel with this operation. Iceland is split by the Cao 2024 static partitions onto plates 102 and 301, and the rigid two-plate pose closes the island to a maximum at about 12 Ma and then RE-OPENS it: past about 13 Ma the eastern half has been carried WNW through the western half and out the far side, so at 16.3 and 20 Ma the reconstructed island is wider than today and its two halves are in the wrong order. Restricting the footprint to the outer flanks is what keeps that artefact tolerable, and it does not remove it. Harardarson et al.'s own arithmetic - 480 km of measured 14-16 Ma separation against 275 km predicted from the spreading rate - also rules out any kinematic back-calculation of the island's width.
ops.claimOrInference: The ages at the NW, N and E localities are claims of the sources. The mapping of those point ages onto areal selectors, and the decision to draw a young-end minimum for a 9 Myr bin, are EarthHistory inferences.
ops.editorial: EarthHistory modification after Saemundsson (1979), Harardarson et al. (2008), the NI 1:600,000 bedrock map and, for the 20-11 lobes, the published Icelandic radiometric age localities

ops.rationale: The paired removal for the 20-11 add-land, for the same reason as the 11-2 pair: the shallow-marine claim must not survive under ground the layer now draws as land. The ring is identical to the add-land, so it covers the three lobes only and leaves Cao's growing Icelandic platform around them untouched.

derivation.sourceLicence: CC BY 4.0, Natturufraedistofnun Islands; the same pinned snapshot the regional Iceland material correction reads, so the two cannot drift
derivation.method: select flokkur='gold', dissolve, drop components below the compiler's 25 km2 piece floor, clip to the three lobe selectors for 20-11 only, simplify 0.02 degrees topology-preserving, round to 4 decimals
derivation.simplificationNote: the memo proposed 0.005 degrees, the material correction's tolerance. 0.02 degrees is used instead because this window is on simplification.json's protected list, so the compiler performs no further node reduction inside it and the contract's own tolerance is the shipped one. 0.02 degrees is 2.2 km, two orders of magnitude inside the declared 60 and 100 km spatial uncertainty, and it is the compiler's own lm baseline.

lobes.note: NW peninsula; >15 Ma at the exposed top, about 16 Ma at the deepest exposed level
N Iceland; about 12 Ma, the weakest of the three and named as such
Eastfjords; 13-14 Ma, 'just over 13 m.y.' at the oldest locality

seamCheck.reason: The Cao 2024 static partitions over Iceland are plate 102 (Greenland) in the west and 301 (Eurasia) in the east, so the palaeo compiler cuts the island on that seam, while the regional Iceland material correction cuts it on the exact shared 101/301 mid-ocean-ridge subsegments. Plates 101 and 102 are measured co-moving to 0.0 km over 0-29 Ma, so the risk is the seam LINE, not the rotations: the two halves of Iceland are carried apart by 210 km by 11 Ma, and ground assigned to the wrong half moves with the wrong plate.
seamCheck.measurement: MEASURED, and it is not agreement. On the four latitudes where both constructions cut through outcrop - 65.4 to 66.0 N - the palaeo 102/301 seam lies 19.7 to 62.2 km EAST of the correction's 101/301 seam. Between 64.6 and 65.2 N the static-partition seam falls inside the neovolcanic gap, where there is no Tertiary outcrop to cut at all, while the ridge line does cut the outcrop; north of 66.0 and south of 65.4 neither cuts it. The declared tolerance is therefore 75 km, set from the measurement rather than from a hope: it is inside the 60 km spatial uncertainty this contract declares for 11-2 and the 100 km for 20-11, and it is larger than Cao's own ~30 km coastline tolerance, which is the part a reader has to be told. Each latitude's separation is pinned above and may not drift by more than 5 km, so the gate catches a change in either construction instead of asserting an agreement that does not exist.
seamCheck.consequence: Iceland's western and eastern halves are drawn on plates that separate with age, and the palaeo land and the gold material outcrop are split on lines up to 62 km apart. At 11 Ma, where the relative displacement reaches 210 km, a 62 km strip of ground rides the opposite plate in one layer from the other. Both layers already declare model inference for every non-modern Iceland pose, and this is one of the reasons.
seamCheck.measuredSeparationNote: Re-derived and re-pinned 2026-09-16, on a corrected measurement. The separation is now measured between the two plates' facing extremities - the west plate's easternmost ground on the parallel against the east plate's westernmost - because the previous rule paired every western segment against every eastern one and kept the smallest gap, which reads interior structure rather than ownership. The previous 65.4/65.6 N values measured a hole wall removed by the compiler-wide ring hygiene, 2026-09-16: a needle hole inside the western ground ended a segment 0.77 km from eastern ground that the compiler's seam buffer had already carried west of it, and that pair won over the real cut. With the needle holes dropped, the old rule found no pair at all on those two parallels, which is how the defect surfaced. The four parallels are unchanged and so is the kind of disagreement this check records: 65.4 N 56.1 -> 62.2 km, 65.6 N 57.5 -> 58.6, 65.8 N 45.5 -> 39.0 and 66.0 N 19.7 -> 19.7, every one still well inside the 75 km tolerance, with the 5 km drift allowance kept rather than widened. The superseded note, from 2026-09-15, recorded the seam buffer moving the same four numbers from 58.0/60.6/40.4/19.7; those were measured on the old rule and are history, not a baseline.

acceptanceAges.reason: The contract's acceptance ages, from the memo's section 5.3 step 9. Each must select the interval named beside it under the half-open (toAgeMa, fromAgeMa] rule the runtime uses (palaeoIntervalCoversAge). Two corrections to the memo's list are pinned here rather than left to be rediscovered: 2.01 and 11.01 Ma are the EXCLUSIVE young bounds of 11-2 and 20-11, so they select nothing and no Iceland land is drawn at either; the youngest age each interval actually covers is the next representable one up. The two negatives are the ages at which nothing here may draw - 1.9 Ma is younger than the whole Cao band, where the layer falls back to today's composition and Iceland is drawn by the native charts, and 20.1 Ma is the interval before this contract starts.

leftAlone.subject: The Jan Mayen microcontinent
leftAlone.reason: A thinned, submerged continental ribbon that became part of Eurasia by 27 Ma, described as 'highly extended or even fragmented', with final dislocation in the Late Oligocene / Early Miocene. The only subaerial volcanism anyone places on it is Eocene, about 55-53 Ma, and the 35-23 Ma uplift and erosion is an unconformity, not a mapped land extent. Cao draws neither lm nor sm over any Jan Mayen witness at either interval and there is no Cao 2024 continental crust there either, so the model already says 'unmapped' - which is the honest answer.

leftAlone.subject: The Faroes and the Iceland-Faroe Ridge land bridge
leftAlone.reason: The contract window deliberately stops at -12 E, west of the Faroe Platform. Three reasons. Cao already draws the Faroes as land at 37-29 and as land plus shallow sea at 29-20, then shallow sea at 20-11 and 11-2, so the model's own GIFR land bridge is Eocene-Oligocene and these two intervals are the ones where Cao has already closed it. The Iceland-Faroe Ridge's structure 'remains ambiguous'. And the transatlantic dispersal events at 9-8 and 5.5 Ma explicitly leave stepping-stone versus continuous open, so a drawn continuous land bridge would assert the stronger of two readings the source does not choose between, across a 1,000 km span, on pollen evidence.

leftAlone.subject: An Icelandic LGM lowstand state
leftAlone.reason: Iceland is outside the LGM contract's three footprints, and a -120 m eustatic contour around Iceland would draw the insular shelf as dry ground at the very age when the Icelandic Ice Sheet covered the island and extended onto that shelf. Adding Iceland to the LGM state needs a cited ice-sheet extent first; a lowstand alone would be worse than the present silence.

leftAlone.subject: The shallow-marine class around Iceland
leftAlone.reason: Cao's Icelandic platform grows through the probe window, which is the right sign for a growing edifice, and nothing retrieved dates a Miocene Icelandic shelf edge. Only the land inside the platform is edited; its outer limit is left exactly as Cao draws it.

leftAlone.subject: The 37-29 Ma Greenland-Iceland-Faroe Ridge landmass
leftAlone.reason: Outside this contract's intervals, it is the model's own reading of the hotspot trail, and the retrieved source states the GIFR 'may have been partly above sea level' - a conditional. Changing it needs its own research round.

notes.rights: The only geometry redistributed here is derived from the Natturufraedistofnun Islands 1:600,000 bedrock map, CC BY 4.0, with attribution, as a modified derivative: dissolved, floored at 25 km2, clipped by EarthHistory's own lobe selectors and simplified. Every publication named is citation-only; no figure, map plate, coordinate list or table from any of them is traced, digitised or reproduced.
notes.frame: Every geometry above is present-day WGS84, like the Cao 2017 source. The compiler cuts it by the Cao 2024 static partitions, which put the western half of Iceland on plate 102 and the eastern half on 301; every resulting pose is model inference, never cited reconstruction, because the rigid two-plate pose closes the island at about 12 Ma and inverts it before that.
notes.presentation: With the palaeo layer on, the regional Iceland material correction (renderOrder 1.5) still draws between palaeo-shallow-marine (1.2) and palaeo-land (1.7). At 11-2 the new palaeo-land ring is built from the same gold geometry the correction's gold:formation chart paints one layer down, in a different colour and with a different meaning: material exists versus this was land. That is a presentation question the map key has to answer explicitly; it is recorded here so it is not discovered on screen.
notes.coverageGap: From 16.3 to 20 Ma the material correction has no chart - 16.3 Ma is its coverage bound, not a birth age - and this contract has no defensible geometry either. Both are silent there, on purpose, and the reason is recorded once here rather than inferred twice.

opSchema.geometry: GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon in present-day WGS84 coordinates, entirely inside the basin window, longitude span below 180 degrees
opSchema.references: at least one entry of this contract's references[], named by sourceId; the compiler rejects an operation without one
opSchema.intervals: every intervalId an operation names must be a canonical Cao interval AND appear in this contract's intervals[]; the operation's intervals must be contiguous in the canonical schedule, and a source record the operation edits may not stay active outside them
opSchema.editorial: must start with 'EarthHistory modification after '; the same prefix is what the emitted evidence record carries
opSchema.replaceRing: replace-ring additionally names targetRecordIndex: the Cao 2017 record whose ring the geometry replaces
opSchema.reporting: the compiler records the area added and removed per operation, per class and per interval, in the emitted catalog
